payload.feature:
This worktree carries decision 0042's second slice on branch fire/0042-sdd-machine: six commits (b13f9c7, 774b1d5, 97a0ca5, e72041e, and two written by the operator by hand, f9f195b and 8d5e6b1) on top of main e2018eb, open as pull request #186 with all thirteen CI checks green. A read-only judging pass on opus then found a HIGH correctness defect and three smaller ones that CI cannot see. This slice answers them on top of the existing commits and ships. Keep every property those six commits established; change nothing else.

FINDING 1, HIGH, correctness and dead policy — quoted from the review: "the `upstream` boundary can never fire in a compiled bundle. engine.rs:1502-1505 takes `final_results` from the last step's results, and engine.rs:1770-1786 ends the sequence only when the word is in the seat's `allowed_results` AND NOT in `final_results`. But bundle.rs:2308-2314 refuses a final step that declares its own `results` and assigns it `results.to_vec()` — the seat's results verbatim — while engine.rs:713/737/802 sets `seq_input["allowed_results"]` to those same seat results. So for every bundle the compiler can produce, `final_results == allowed_results` and `ends_sequence` is identically false. Consequence: when `specify:author`, `design:chief` or `tasks:author` reports `upstream` (its declared vocabulary in recipes/triage/bundle.json:77,114,129), the result is only checkpointed and the sequence runs on into the dialect validator, whose exec can only report `drafted` or `fail`. On design and tasks `openspec validate {change} --strict` will normally still pass, so the phase reports `drafted` and the machine advances to the next artifact phase carrying the fault the author just declared — fail-open past a declared defect. On specify there is usually no change to expand, so the run parks as indeterminate instead of under SPECIFY-UPSTREAM. Five of the twenty-four shipped rules are therefore unreachable: SPECIFY-UPSTREAM, DESIGN-UPSTREAM, DESIGN-UPSTREAM-EXHAUSTED, TASKS-UPSTREAM, TASKS-UPSTREAM-EXHAUSTED, against ruling 2's '`upstream` returns to the previous artifact phase under a visits bound' and its own enforcement binding. The green suite does not say this: the only test that drives an `upstream` result (engine/tests.rs:4121-4185) hand-builds a final step whose results are ["drafted","fail"] while the seat's are ["drafted","fail","upstream"] — a shape parse_sequence cannot emit."

Make an author step's `upstream` end its sequence and become the seat's result, so the five rules are reachable and a declared fault can never be walked past. Decide the mechanism yourself and say why in the commit: the engine may compare against the vocabulary the remaining steps can actually emit rather than against the seat's own, or the compiler may record each step's emitted vocabulary for the engine to read. Whatever you choose must fail closed: a word the seat declares and no later step can produce ends the sequence there. The proof is the part that was missing — a machine-proof scenario that drives the REAL compiled `recipes/triage` design route (not a hand-built sequence) so that an author step reports `upstream`, and asserts the run re-enters the previous artifact phase, and a second pass at the bound asserts the exhausted rule. Replace or extend engine/tests.rs:4121-4185 so no test relies on a shape `parse_sequence` cannot emit.

FINDING 2, LOW, fit — quoted: "the retry bound is real but counts returns, not failures. `visits_specify_gte: 2` conflates the one permitted re-run with every other edge into the phase: CLARIFY-AMBIGUOUS, DESIGN-UPSTREAM, ANALYZE-DRIFT-SPECIFY and both REVIEW-*-SPEC-DEFECT rules all re-enter specify. After a single clarify return, a first-ever validate `fail` matches SPECIFY-FAIL-TWICE and hard-stops with no retry, where ruling 2 says '`fail` re-enters the phase once, then stops'." Make the bound count what the ruling means. If the closed condition vocabulary cannot express "failures at this phase" without a new key, say so plainly in the commit and leave the conflation with a comment naming it, rather than inventing a key this slice was not commissioned to add; if it can, fix it and add a table test that mixes a loop return with a first failure.

FINDING 3, LOW and SECURITY, injection through seat results — quoted: "the `{change}` fence reads backwards inside a sequence. engine.rs:1798-1819 validates `inputs.change` against ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$ only when `declares_change` is true, but adopts the value into `nearest_change` either way, and `nearest_change` is substituted into the next dialect step's argv by expand_dialect_argv. A seat that does not declare `change` therefore passes an unvalidated string — `--config=...`, `../../..` — straight into the tool's argv. Not reachable in the shipped bundles, so it is latent, and argv is execed without a shell — but the value is validated only when declared and used whether declared or not. The new test's 'an input the seat did not declare is ignored' only exercises `42`, which `as_str()` drops for an unrelated reason; a string sails through." Validate unconditionally, or ignore an undeclared claim outright; the test must drive a STRING through the undeclared path and prove it never reaches an argv.

FINDING 4, LOW, fit — quoted: "the deterministic half of each loop is enforced only by charter prose. Because of the mechanism in finding 1, a `check` step reporting `ambiguous`/`drift` cannot end the sequence; it lands in `context.prior_results.check` and the clean exit depends on the judge honouring analyst.md / clarifier.md." Finding 1's fix should give the check step the same teeth; prove it with a test where the deterministic check reports a non-zero count and the phase does not advance whatever the judge says.

TWO INFO RIDERS. The `brokkr recipes list` sample in docs/guides/recipe-authoring.md gives `research b9a38128ef56` and `research-dsh 78a785cface7` while witness_digests.rs pins different values for those two recipes; regenerate the sample from the binary so the guide matches the pins. And `dialects/speckit.json`'s validate and check argv name `brokkr dialect check ...`, a subcommand the CLI does not have — either add nothing and mark it `unsupported` with the measured reason, as the dialect vocabulary allows, or name the command that exists; do not ship an argv that cannot run. Leave the pre-existing `library_path` spelling gap alone: it is main's, not this branch's, and it wants its own slice.

Constraints: the exact coverage gate (scripts/coverage-exact.sh, run with stdin closed: </dev/null) must stay at literal 100%; clippy -D warnings and fmt must stay clean; cargo test --workspace green here and inside a box (`BROKKR_HANDS_BOX` guards every box-opening test); contracts/ existing files, fixtures/ and policy/phase-machine.json are read-only; every test that compares a reported path against a built path compares them as `Path`s or canonicalized, never as strings with a separator inside a component, and paths inside a hands box are POSIX strings; a guide this slice touches is revised, never gutted; the decision index docs/decisions/README.md must keep every row main carries in number order; do not name the private neighbours in prose; commit in the repository's style on top of 8d5e6b1 and never push.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

result.notes: Implemented and committed 4e2d1dd: compiled dialect steps now retain their actual result vocabulary, unreachable upstream and deterministic-check boundaries fail closed, artifact retries count consecutive phase failures, undeclared change strings cannot reach dialect argv, and unsupported spec-kit commands plus recipe-list digests are corrected. cargo test --workspace, boxed hands tests, fmt, clippy -D warnings, bundles/self compilation, and exact 100% line/branch/function coverage all pass.

cargo test --workspace: 60 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

Reviewed 4e2d1dd (the run's only commit) against 8d5e6b1. Findings 1, 2 and 3 are answered well; finding 4's fix introduces a HIGH correctness regression on the analyze route. Gates I could run are green: cargo test --workspace, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings, cargo fmt --check, `brokkr compile --bundle bundles/self`. `brokkr recipes list` output is byte-exact with the docs/guides/recipe-authoring.md sample (info rider 1 done). docs/decisions/README.md carries 44 rows, same as main. contracts/, fixtures/, policy/phase-machine.json and reference/ are untouched by the whole branch. I could NOT run scripts/coverage-exact.sh: the seat sandbox refused the command, so the literal-100% constraint is unverified here and rests on CI.

RESIDUAL 1 - HIGH, correctness, regression this commit introduced. The analyze loop's deterministic drift now parks the run unruled. engine.rs:1783-1789 (`failed_check`) makes the compiled analyze `check` step's `drift` end the sequence, so the `judge` (the analyst) never runs. The analyst is the only source of `drift_in`: recipes/triage/bundle.json declares `analyze.inputs = ["drift_in"]`, and the dialect exec adapter's result (adapters.rs:2242-2248) carries only result/inputs.change/notes/model/effort - never drift_in. All three routing rules ANALYZE-DRIFT-SPECIFY / -DESIGN / -TASKS require `drift_in`, and ANALYZE-DRIFT-EXHAUSTED requires visits_analyze>=3. On the first analyze visit an absent drift_in yields Ok(false) at policy.rs:579, no rule matches, and policy.rs:237 returns NoRule{problem:None} -> engine.rs:2077 journals rule_id:null, next:null, "no rule matched". Live on this repository's own realm: dialects/openspec.json declares analyze.check = `openspec status --change {change} --json`, and sdd_shape.rs:113-116 pins the compiled analyze seat as exactly [check(Dialect), judge]. night-shift inherits it. Before this commit the check's `drift` was checkpointed and the analyst ran and supplied drift_in, so this is a regression, not a pre-existing gap. The new test only drives clarify, where CLARIFY-AMBIGUOUS has no `when` and so routes fine. Finding 4 asked that the judge not be able to erase a proven count; ending the sequence also discards the classification the table needs. A narrower mechanism (refuse a judge result that erases the check's non-zero finding, or require drift_in from the judge) would keep the route. Fails closed (a park, not a fail-open), so no security implication.

RESIDUAL 2 - LOW, simplicity. The "record the emitted vocabulary" mechanism is duplicated and not universal. bundle.rs:2423-2428 and engine.rs:58-65 hold the same phase->(success,failure) table with no test binding them (divergence fails loudly at engine.rs:1745, so it is fragility, not a hole). More to the point, the synthesised verify sequence at bundle.rs:1136 still gives its `dialect-verify` step `results.clone()` - the seat's results verbatim, exactly the shape finding 1 named as wrong - so the commit message's invariant does not hold for every compiled dialect step. Benign today because every shipped verify seat is ["pass","fail"]; a verify seat declaring a third word would reopen the same fail-open in the verify lane.

RESIDUAL 3 - LOW, fit. FAILURE_RESULTS was widened globally (fold.rs:18) but its doc comment still claims the list matches "the production table's retry/hard-stop rules"; `fail` matches no production-table rule. I checked every table: no phase both emits `fail` and reads consecutive_failures_gte except the new SDD phases, so no routing changed. But `verify` failures in fast/node/panel-review/preflight/research/self now increment the counter and surface in decision inputs and the readouts (brokkr-view, ui.rs, muninn.rs) - a journal-shape change beyond the commission. Finding 2 itself is otherwise correctly answered: consecutive_failures gives ruling 2's "fail re-enters once, then stops" per streak, a clarify or upstream return resets it, and policy/tests.rs mixes visits=9 with cf=1/2 as the commission asked.

INFO - dialects/speckit.json marking specify.validate `unsupported` converts a runtime failure into a compile refusal: bundle.rs:2377 errors on an unsupported `validate`, while an unsupported `check` is merely skipped at 2374. A realm declaring speckit can therefore no longer compile recipes/triage at all, though decision 0042 offers speckit as one of two measured dialects. Fail-closed and better than shipping an argv that cannot run, but it is a capability change worth the operator's ruling.

SECURITY - none above info. Finding 3 is genuinely closed. I traced the newly-live `ends_sequence` early return (engine.rs:1791), which skips the in-sequence change validation at 1804, but decide() independently validates a declared `change` (engine.rs:1876-1886) and inputs.retain (engine.rs:1921) drops an undeclared one before it reaches phase_results, so no unvalidated string can reach nearest_change or expand_dialect_argv. The revised test drives a real string (--config=../../..) through the undeclared path and proves the dialect step never receives an argv. No journal tamper path, no protocol confusion, no secrets touched; the upstream and retry-bound changes both tighten fail-closed behaviour.

Committed 01413b4 atop 4e2d1dd. Deterministic clarify/analyze failures now remain enforced while the analyze judge supplies drift_in; contradictory clean judgments park. Compiler and engine share the dialect result vocabulary, synthesized verify steps no longer inherit impossible seat results, and SDD fail counting is scoped to phases whose rules read consecutive_failures so unrelated verify journals remain unchanged. Workspace tests pass normally and with BROKKR_HANDS_BOX=1; fmt, clippy -D warnings, bundles/self compilation, and exact 100% line/branch/function coverage pass.

cargo test --workspace: 60 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

Reviewed 8d5e6b1..01413b4 (two commits, 15 files) against the four findings and two riders. All four are answered and the mechanism is sound; four LOW residuals remain, none security.

WHAT I VERIFIED. cargo test --workspace green at HEAD; cargo fmt --check clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; compile --bundle bundles/self green (digest d06e486c3ef8). Read-only paths untouched: contracts/, fixtures/, policy/phase-machine.json and docs/decisions/README.md are unchanged in the run's diff. Two commits ahead of origin, nothing pushed. The exact coverage gate I could NOT re-run: the root filesystem is at 100% (5.4G free) and my instrumented build died with a linker bus error; I removed the 4.5G target/llvm-cov-target I had created. I verified it instead from target/coverage/coverage-summary.json and lcov.info written at 16:29 on the final tree (they carry Machine::reads_counter, added by 01413b4): lines 19224/19224, branches 3052/3052, functions 1825/1825 — literal 100%. The boxed suite was run by the verify phase inside the hands box (60 suite summaries, 0 failed); this seat's shell cannot set BROKKR_HANDS_BOX.

FINDING 1 (HIGH) — CLOSED. The compiler now records a dialect step's real emitted vocabulary (bundle.rs dialect_results, applied both to a parsed dialect step and to the synthesized dialect-verify) and the engine compares an intermediate result against the remaining steps rather than the seat's own. On the compiled specify/design/tasks routes the final validate step is ['drafted','fail'], so an author's 'upstream' now ends the sequence and becomes the seat result; the five rules are reachable. The proof drives the REAL compiled recipes/triage design seat, asserts the validator never ran, and rules DESIGN-UPSTREAM to specify and DESIGN-UPSTREAM-EXHAUSTED at the bound. The hand-built shape parse_sequence cannot emit is gone. I checked the widening for new bypasses: 'pass' from the design positions panel is not seat-declared, 'fail' is still emittable by validate, review's chief is final with the seat's results, and verify's dialect-verify vocabulary equals its seat's — no shipped path skips a gate into ship.

FINDING 2 (LOW) — CLOSED. SPECIFY/DESIGN/TASKS-FAIL-TWICE now read consecutive_failures_gte:2; the engine computes the counter for exactly the phases whose rules read it and the fold counts a 'fail' only when that engine-written input is present. A clarify return followed by a first-ever validate failure now takes SPECIFY-RETRY (table test mixes visits_specify:9 with consecutive_failures:1). Removing the visits bound opens no thrash hole: every edge back into specify carries its own bound (visits_clarify 3, visits_specify 3, visits_analyze 3).

FINDING 3 (LOW, SECURITY) — CLOSED. An undeclared 'change' claim is now dropped outright before it can reach nearest_change, and the test drives the string '--config=../../..' through the undeclared path and proves the dialect step refuses with 'no preceding successful result carries it' rather than expanding an argv. I also chased the cross-phase source: nearest_change() reads the journal, and decide() both drops undeclared keys and identifier-validates a declared 'change', so no unvalidated string reaches argv by that route either. Separately I confirmed the fold's new presence-triggered increment cannot be driven by a seat: consecutive_failures is in ENGINE_OWNED_INPUTS, compilation refuses a seat that declares it, and decide() strips it before the engine's own overlay.

FINDING 4 (LOW) — CLOSED. A deterministic clarify/analyze check reporting its failure word is remembered, and a final judge that answers with the phase's clean word parks the effect indeterminate naming both steps; the clean-check and the analyze drift-classification paths still pass through. The charter is no longer the only boundary.

RIDER 1 — CLOSED. `brokkr recipes list` output now matches the guide sample on all twelve rows byte for byte, and the four moved digests (night-shift 1fa050796f20, triage 2bc18b05f87a, research 50c7db63c6f5, research-dsh 2095631397be) match witness_digests.rs. RIDER 2 — CLOSED. No `brokkr dialect check` argv remains in dialects/speckit.json; both sites carry `unsupported` with a measured reason.

RESIDUAL FINDINGS (all LOW, none security, none fixed by me):

1. LOW, dead policy — bundle.rs parse_sequence refuses a FINAL step that declares 'results' but silently discards a DIALECT step's declared 'results' after parsing and validating them. recipes/triage/bundle.json still carries "results":["clear","ambiguous"] and ["consistent","drift"] on the two check steps, now inert data; an author who wrote ["nonsense"] there would compile clean and get the dialect's vocabulary instead. The two cases should be refused the same way, or the key kept and checked against dialect_results.

2. LOW, fit — Machine::reads_counter is scoped to the phase, not to the result. A table where one phase carries a counter-guarded rule on one result and an unguarded 'fail' rule on another would silently feed the SDD counter from that unrelated 'fail' and hard-stop the guarded result a visit early. No shipped table has that shape (consecutive_failures_gte appears only on implement/architecture with broken/failed, and on the three SDD phases with fail), so it is latent — but the doc comment claims the counter is computed 'without changing unrelated journals that happen to use the same word', which is only true because no shipped table mixes them.

3. LOW, fit — marking spec-kit's specify validator `unsupported` makes the shipped SDD recipes refuse to COMPILE in a spec-kit realm: parse_sequence only `continue`s past an unsupported `check`; an unsupported `validate` on an artifact phase is a hard CompileError. Before this slice such a realm compiled and failed at exec with a nonexistent subcommand, so the new behaviour is fail-closed and better — but it retires a shipped dialect's SDD route, and neither the commit message nor a test says so.

4. LOW, test coverage — the upstream proof is a compiled-bundle unit test in engine/tests.rs, not a machine_proof run: it fabricates visits_specify in a synthetic RunState instead of letting the fold count phase/entered, and asserts decide()'s ruling rather than the run's re-entry. machine_proof.rs still contains no 'upstream' scenario at all. specify and tasks upstream reachability (their validate step's narrowed vocabulary) and analyze's contradiction arm are proven only by the shared code path, not by their own assertions.

TWO INFO OBSERVATIONS, not findings. (a) The new boundary law is general: any earlier step that reports a seat-declared word no later step can emit now skips every remaining step, gates included. In the shipped bundles that is only 'upstream' skipping the artifact validator, which is right — there is no artifact to validate — and no shipped sequence lets a work step skip a gate on the way to ship. Worth stating in the decision when 0042 is next revised. (b) If a verify seat ever declared a result beyond pass/fail, its `checks` step reporting that word would now end the sequence before the dialect validator; the new bundle test pins the narrowed dialect-verify vocabulary but not that consequence.
